properties.biography: Mitski Miyawaki (born Mitsuki Laycock) was born in 1990 in Mie Prefecture, Japan, to a Japanese mother and an American father. Because her father worked for the U.S. Department of State, her family moved frequently and she spent parts of her childhood in Turkey, China, Malaysia, the Czech Republic and the Democratic Republic of Congo before ultimately moving to the United States. She sang in choirs in school and began composing on piano as a teenager. While studying studio composition at Purchase College, she self-released two albums, Lush (2012) and Retired from Sad, New Career in Business (2013), which began as senior projects. Mitski's breakthrough came with the rawer, guitar-forward Bury Me at Makeout Creek (2014). After signing to Dead Oceans she released Puberty 2 (2016), Be the Cowboy (2018) and Laurel Hell (2022), earning critical acclaim, festival headline slots and a growing global fanbase. In 2023 she released The Land Is Inhospitable and So Are We. Her songwriting has been praised for its candor, dramatic dynamics and vivid, emotionally calibrated narratives.

properties.description: Mitski (born Mitsuki Laycock; also known as Mitski Miyawaki) is a Japanese-American singer-songwriter whose work blends indie rock, art-pop and confessional songwriting. She studied studio composition at Purchase College, self-releasing two early albums as student projects before gaining wider attention with 2014's Bury Me at Makeout Creek. After signing to Dead Oceans in 2015, she released critically acclaimed albums including Puberty 2 (2016), Be the Cowboy (2018) and Laurel Hell (2022). Mitski's songwriting is noted for its emotional directness, striking imagery and dramatic dynamics; she has received widespread critical praise and earned an Academy Award nomination for co-writing "This Is a Life" (Everything Everywhere All at Once).

Her Academy Award nomination and mainstream press coverage have also raised her profile beyond indie circles.

properties.biography: Born Claire Cottrill on August 18, 1998 in Carlisle, Massachusetts, Clairo began making and uploading songs as a teenager. She broke out in late 2017 when a homemade video for "Pretty Girl" went viral on YouTube, bringing widespread attention to her bedroom-pop sound. In 2018 she compiled early singles on the EP Diary 001. Her debut studio album Immunity (2019), featuring production and co-writing from Rostam Batmanglij, expanded her sound and garnered critical acclaim. Sling (2021), co-produced with Jack Antonoff, marked a stylistic evolution toward richer arrangements; Charm (2024), produced with Leon Michels, continued her artistic growth. Throughout, her lyrics have focused on coming-of-age themes, mental health and sexuality while maintaining a DIY, intimate aesthetic.
